entries.original_title: Correspondence of the brain's functional architecture during activation and rest
entries.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
entries.description: Resting-state brain networks correspond to the functional networks engaged during task performance.
entries.citation_sentence: In 2009, Smith et al. published a paper in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 30 that showed that the collection of brain networks that are 'active' while a person is resting and engaged in idle thought (e.g., resting state networks or RSNs) correspond to the same functional networks used by the brain to perform tasks.
entries.notes: The paper explicitly states that the Smith et al. findings were highly reproducible and that this study provided a true replication, while also noting differences in subjects, stimuli, data inputs, and analysis methods.
